title: TERRA-X · Elegí el mundo visual
question: The roll assigned the Meridian Wall. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Meridian Wall
options.lineage: Sundials and cathedral meridian lines: reading the Sun from the shadow it casts
options.thesis: The page is a sunlit wall: move the Sun and every element casts a real, measurable shadow.
options.viewport: Huge expanded headline on the wall casting a long hard shadow; Mons Mouton relief set in as a basalt plate with hairline callouts; the Sun scale (1.5° to 10°) as the gnomon control; one ink plaque button: Explore a candidate.
options.risk: Warm plaster can read as heritage instead of space science if the data plates are not crisp.

raised.raise: The horizon line is the page's threshold: below it, night is held as unmarked dark, like a permanently shadowed crater.
Data sections run one measurement per full-width row, ruled like chalk marks.
Every object in the 3D relief and the diagrams wears a small printed label on a hairline pointer.

options.label: Lunar Topographic Chart
options.thesis: Every screen is a sheet of a lunar chart: shaded relief, contours, grid ticks and marginal legends.
options.viewport: A chart sheet with the relief as the main map, title block and legend in the margin, the action in the legend.
options.risk: Familiar: hairline chart aesthetics are where many science sites land.

options.label: Accretion Disk Threshold
options.thesis: Matter crossing an irreversible horizon, rendered as glowing rings.
options.viewport: A warped glowing disk around a black center, labels orbiting the rim.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a black hole misstates the Moon's physics; the jury would read spectacle, not grazing light.
options.risk: Generic space spectacle that hides the product.
options.kept: The threshold as the organizing line, night held as unmarked dark.

options.label: Blacksmith Scale Shower
options.thesis: Each blow lengthens the bar with brutal clarity.
options.viewport: One strike per full-width row with force numerals.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in TERRA-X is forged; audience and clarity both lose.
options.risk: Industrial costume with no link to the Moon.
options.kept: One measurement per full-width row, ruled like chalk marks.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Data sublime in pure black and white.
options.viewport: A wall of hairline bars and dense numbers.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dazzling but opaque; a jury would not learn what an analog is.
options.kept: Total commitment to two inks and tabular numbers.

options.label: Nixie Laboratory Counter
options.thesis: Every quantity glows inside its own glass tube.
options.viewport: Banks of glowing digits for hours of night and battery.
options.case: Fuses partly: the lab's numbers fit, but light and shadow, the core idea, get lost.
options.kept: Each key quantity owns a fixed tabular slot that never reflows.

options.label: Arcade Marquee Row
options.viewport: A dark aisle of glowing cabinets.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful arcade tone undercuts a scientific claim.
options.risk: Reads as a game, not as evidence.
options.kept: The active destination clearly holds its light in the navigation.

options.label: Busytown Cross-Section
options.thesis: A cutaway world where every object wears a label.
options.case: Fuses poorly: childlike register for a NASA jury.
options.risk: Too cute for a science demo.
options.kept: Every object wears a small printed label on a hairline pointer.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A space-tech landing page executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Dark hero with a planet image, headline left, cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every space hackathon project by design.
